title: Measurability of the Rademacher matrix map
statement: Equip the sample space $\Omega = \{\omega : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathrm{Fin}\,d \to \bbr\}$ of $k \times d$ real arrays with its product $\sigma$-algebra, and the space $\bbr^{k \times d}$ of matrices likewise. Then the map $A : \Omega \to \bbr^{k\times d}$ sending $\omega$ to the matrix with entries $A(\omega)_{ij} = \omega_{ij}/\sqrt{k}$ is measurable.
hypotheses_covered: k, d : ℕ are the matrix dimensions
domain is RadΩ(k,d) with product σ-algebra
codomain is matrices over ℝ with product σ-algebra
replaced:
The map $\omega \mapsto \mathrm{radMatrix}(k,d,\omega)$ is measurable with
respect to the product $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathrm{Rad\Omega}(k,d)$.
